problem: Object-navigation agents are trained on a fixed set of common categories and need millions of in-domain simulation steps. Prior zero-shot ObjectNav methods (EmbCLIP-ZSON, SemanticNav-ZSON) still train per simulator. No benchmark tested finding objects from free-form language (uncommon objects, attribute descriptions with distractors, hidden objects) without navigation training.
motivation: Robots should find arbitrary objects that people describe, such as a lost 'toy airplane', in unknown environments, with no in-domain navigation training. Open-vocabulary image models (CLIP, OWL-ViT, MDETR) already classify, detect and segment arbitrary text-specified objects. The paper asks how far these models get on an embodied task when simply combined with classical mapping and exploration, and without any fine-tuning.
key_idea: CLIP on Wheels (CoW) is a modular, training-free agent: it explores with a classical frontier-based policy until a frozen open-vocabulary localizer fires on the language goal, then plans to the back-projected goal location on a depth-built top-down map. The paper pairs CoW with a new benchmark, PASTURE, for language-driven zero-shot object navigation (L-ZSON).
insight:
Open-vocabulary localizers inherit web-scale concept knowledge, which is why the best CoW (OWL-ViT B/32 with post-processing) finds uncommon PASTURE objects more often than common RoboTHOR ones (32.8 vs 26.7 SR). However, CoWs cannot exploit attribute or spatial language: appearance and spatial descriptions fall below their RoboTHOR baseline, and distractors hurt further. Failure analysis attributes errors mostly to exploration and object localization, with more localization failures when distractors are present. Ablations show:
- Registering only the center pixel of detections generally helps.
- ViT-B/16 is no better, and often worse, than ViT-B/32 (especially for CLIP).
- OWL-ViT is the best localizer.
- Removing min-max normalization from Chefer-style gradient relevance gives a usable true-negative signal.
- The frontier-exploration heuristic beats explorers trained with DD-PPO for 60M steps (Table 2: RoboTHOR SR 26.7 FBE vs 20.9 RoboTHOR-trained vs 20.4 Habitat-trained).
- The 80-template prompt ensemble matters little (SPL 9.7 vs 9.5).
method: Depth-based mapping: builds a 0.125 m top-down free/occupied grid by back-projecting egocentric depth. Pose comes from dead-reckoning the intended action deltas using known intrinsics and agent height (0.9 m). Failed actions are detected from depth-frame differences (mean/std thresholds 0.1 m), and the map is re-initialized when no frontier is reachable.

Exploration: the default is frontier-based exploration (Yamauchi), which greedily moves to the nearest free/unknown frontier. The learnable alternative is a frozen CLIP backbone with a GRU and actor/critic heads, trained with DD-PPO (AllenAct) for 60M steps on RoboTHOR or MP3D train scenes. Its count-based reward gives +0.1 per new 0.125 m voxel and -0.01 per step.

Object localization (zero-shot, frozen): (1) CLIP-Ref, which matches the image against k=9 referring expressions for image regions; (2) CLIP-Patch, which runs CLIP on k=9 image patches; (3) CLIP-Grad, which uses Chefer et al. ViT relevance with the normalization removed so relevance stays low when the target is absent; (4) MDETR fine-tuned on PhraseCut for segmentation; (5) OWL-ViT open-vocabulary detection. CLIP variants use the 80-template ImageNet prompt ensemble.

Post-processing: continuous scores are thresholded into binary masks. Thresholds are grid-searched to maximize macro-F1 on 500 rendered RoboTHOR and 500 Habitat MP3D train-scene images; PASTURE reuses the RoboTHOR thresholds. Either the full mask or only the mask's center pixel is registered.
Target-driven planning: 2D relevance is back-projected into the map, keeping the max per cell. Once confidence exceeds the threshold, the agent plans to the high-relevance cell and issues STOP.

PASTURE benchmark: built on 15 RoboTHOR validation rooms, with 12 objects per room and 2 start poses, giving 2,520 episodes. It has 7 tasks: uncommon objects (12 CGTrader assets); appearance descriptions ('{size}, {color}, {material} {object}'); spatial descriptions ('on top of x, near y'); both of these with distractor instances; hidden objects ('under/in' a large object); and hidden objects with visible distractors.

setting.backbone: Frozen open-vocabulary localizers (OWL-ViT, CLIP, MDETR; ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16 or EfficientNet-B3) + frontier-based exploration heuristic; optional learned explorer (frozen CLIP + GRU, DD-PPO)
setting.model_size: ViT-B/32 / ViT-B/16 / EfficientNet-B3 scale localizers (parameter counts not stated)
setting.training_data: none (training-free) for default FBE CoWs. Detection thresholds are tuned on 500 rendered images from each of the RoboTHOR and Habitat MP3D train scenes. Optional learned-exploration ablations train 60M DD-PPO steps on RoboTHOR or MP3D train scenes with a count-based reward.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D; pose estimated by dead-reckoning of intended actions (no GPS/compass); known camera intrinsics and agent height
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, ROTATE_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP
setting.privileged: none (pose from action dead-reckoning; RoboTHOR has actuation noise, Habitat has depth noise)

numbers_note: Numbers on the MP3D and RoboTHOR validation sets come from their use as test sets. The abstract and text claim a 15.6-point SR gain over EmbCLIP-ZSON on the RoboTHOR subset, but Table 3 gives 32.5 (OWL) and 23.7 (CLIP-Grad.) vs 14.0 for EmbCLIP-ZSON, i.e. 18.5 and 9.7 points; the claim is likely left over from an earlier version. The EmbCLIP-ZSON number is marked as partly non-zero-shot. Category-level results (Tables 7-12) and failure breakdowns (Figs. 6, 14) exist but are not transcribed. Habitat-learned exploration (Table 2) gives PASTURE SPL 8.6 / SR 19.4 and RoboTHOR SPL 9.8 / SR 20.4.
results: The best CoW (OWL-ViT B/32, center-pixel post-processing, frontier exploration) reaches 21.1 average SR / 12.6 SPL on PASTURE and 26.7 SR / 16.9 SPL on RoboTHOR val with zero navigation training. It finds uncommon objects at 32.8 SR but drops to 14.4-16.1 SR on distractor tasks. On the RoboTHOR ZSON subset it gets 32.5 SR vs 14.0 for EmbCLIP-ZSON (60M training steps). On Habitat MP3D, CoW CLIP-Grad. B/32 matches SemanticNav-ZSON in SPL (4.9 vs 4.8; 500M training steps) but trails it in SR (9.2 vs 15.3). A supervised ProcTHOR fine-tuned agent remains far stronger on RoboTHOR (66.4 SR).
limitations: No large-scale real-world benchmarking; evaluation is simulation only (RoboTHOR, Habitat MP3D, PASTURE).

Inherits the limits of its localizers and explorers: per-domain confidence thresholds must be tuned for precision/recall, and attribute/spatial language and distractors are poorly exploited. Absolute success is low, especially on MP3D (≤9.2 SR).
Only a single LoCoBot embodiment with discrete actions; continuous actions and other morphologies are not studied.
